answer: One strong defence is a refundable stake bonded to each identity: an agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it runs duplicate accounts. Like a walnut, the shell is cheap to crack open once but expensive to grow again, so creating a hundred fake inlets costs a hundred deposits while honest agents pay nothing beyond the lock. Reputation then builds like a mesa, rising only on identities with stake at risk, so an attacker must fund every fake and the cost scales with the size of the attack.
